verses.text: A few days later, Jesus went back to Capernaum. People heard that he had come home.
So many people gathered that there was no room left, not even outside the door. And Jesus taught them God's message.
Then four men came, carrying a man who could not move his body.
They could not get him close to Jesus because of the crowd. So they made a hole in the roof above Jesus. Then they let the man down through the hole, lying on his mat.
When Jesus saw their faith, he said to the man, "Son, your sins are forgiven."
Some teachers of the law were sitting there. They thought to themselves,
"Why does this man talk like that? He is insulting God! Only God can forgive sins!"
Straight away Jesus knew in his spirit what they were thinking. He said to them, "Why are you thinking these things?
Which is easier to say to this man? Is it easier to say, 'Your sins are forgiven'? Or to say, 'Get up, pick up your mat and walk'?
But I want you to know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins." So he said to the man,
"I tell you, get up, pick up your mat and go home."
The man got up, picked up his mat straight away and walked out while everyone watched. They were all amazed, and they praised God. They said, "We have never seen anything like this!"
Jesus went out beside the lake again. A large crowd came to him, and he began to teach them.
As he walked along, he saw Levi, the son of Alphaeus, sitting at the tax office. "Follow me," Jesus said to him. Levi got up and followed him.
Later, Jesus was having a meal at Levi's house. Many tax collectors and sinners were eating with Jesus and his followers, because many of them followed him.
Some teachers of the law who were Pharisees saw him eating with sinners and tax collectors. They asked his followers, "Why does he eat and drink with tax collectors and sinners?"

Jesus heard this and said to them, "People who are healthy do not need a doctor. Sick people do. I have not come to call people who think they are good. I have come to call sinners to turn away from their sins."
John's followers and the Pharisees were fasting. Some people came and asked Jesus, "John's followers and the followers of the Pharisees are fasting. Why are your followers not fasting?"
Jesus answered, "How can the guests at a wedding fast while the bridegroom is with them? They cannot fast while he is still with them.
But the time will come when the bridegroom will be taken away from them. Then they will fast.
"No one sews a patch of new cloth on old clothes. If they do, the new patch will shrink and pull away from the old cloth. Then the hole will be worse.
And no one pours new wine into old wineskins. If they do, the wine will burst the skins, and both the wine and the skins will be ruined. No, they pour new wine into new wineskins."
One Sabbath day Jesus was walking through the grain fields. As his followers walked along, they began to pick some ears of grain.
The Pharisees said to him, "Look! Why are they doing what is not allowed on the Sabbath?"
Jesus answered, "Have you never read what David did when he and his men were hungry and needed food?
When Abiathar was the high priest, David went into the house of God and ate the holy bread. Only priests were allowed to eat it. And he also gave some to his men."
Then Jesus said to them, "The Sabbath was made for people. People were not made for the Sabbath.
So the Son of Man is Lord even of the Sabbath."
